newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Ingosstrakh to expand medical insurance.
newsitem.headline: Russia Ingosstrakh to expand medical insurance.

text.p: A top official of Russia's second biggest insurer, SAO Ingosstrakh, said on Monday it planned to expand its medical insurance services programme and could more than double its branch network.

"In the strategic development of Ingosstrakh we see personal insurance as a long-term goal," said Fyodor Prokopov, vice-president of Ingosstrakh, which specialises in insuring ships and branches of Russian companies outside of Russia.
He told a news conference that the company could more than double its branch network from a current 60 offices in the Commonwealth of Independent States and abroad.
"I can see nothing bad in Ingosstrakh growing to 120 or 150 branches," he said. He did not name a time frame for the expansion.
"We are sure that the further development of insurance services in the Russian Federation is connected to the development of personal medical insurance," he added.
Prokopov said his company would be satisfied with a 10 percent share of the Russian personal medical insurance market, which is dominated by Russia's biggest insurer, Rosgosstrakh.
Medical insurance premiums paid to Ingosstrakh doubled in 1996 over 1995, though they did not make more than five percent of the company's total premiums, he said.
He said Ingosstrakh had started a programme for personal insurance, Above Barriers, this autumn for medium and large Russian businesses.
The plan included treatment in Swiss hospitals, with whom Ingosstrakh had recently signed agreements, he said.
Ingosstrakh plans to improve access to regional markets by cooperation with and acquisition of regional insurance companies, Prokopov said.
